strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with clear impact on LRM inference efficiency; concrete example (50GB KV cache) effectively demonstrates the bottleneck
Novel insight that attention sparsity patterns reveal distinct thought types (R/E/T) with empirically validated importance hierarchy (R>E>T), supported by counterfactual analysis
Comprehensive algorithm-system co-design combining TBQ, TBE, and CT kernel; analysis of gather overhead (37× TPOT slowdown) effectively motivates custom kernel
Strong empirical results: <5% KV cache with near-lossless accuracy, 5.8× throughput gains, consistent across multiple LRM families and diverse benchmarks
Thorough experimental evaluation with appropriate baselines, multiple datasets, extensive ablations (Tables 3-4, Figures 9-10), and careful analysis of accuracy-compression tradeoffs
Excellent reproducibility support: detailed pseudocode, walkthrough examples, implementation specifics, and comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Heuristic thought decomposition methodology lacks theoretical justification: why attention sparsity must correlate with thought importance is assumed but unproven; Figure 13 shows some models have indistinguishable sparsity boundaries
Fixed |T|=3 assumption appears model-specific; generalization to standard LLMs with |T|=1 shows only modest improvements (Table 10), undermining universality claims

Critical design choices lack principled justification: precision assignment (8/4/2-bit) appears hand-tuned, retention schedule R={64,32,16,8,4} and refresh interval τ=128 chosen empirically without deeper analysis of sensitivity

Insufficient theoretical understanding of hybrid quantization-eviction synergy: Figure 2 shows empirically that hybrid outperforms pure approaches, but the mechanism ('regularizing quantization-induced length inflation') is vague and unanalyzed

Experimental fairness concerns: ThinKV uses custom Triton kernel while baselines use FlashAttention-2; acknowledged as 'proof of concept' (E.2); throughput gains may reflect kernel quality rather than algorithmic superiority; iso-batch comparison limited to single batch size

RoPE-induced key drift concerns in K-means clustering inadequately addressed: §D.4 argues drift negligible within 128-token segments but provides no empirical validation; recommended Windowed RoPE fix not evaluated
Limited generalization beyond LRMs: approach designed specifically for reasoning; weak performance on standard LLM long-response task (LongWriter); no evaluation on other long-output applications
Missing ablations: no direct comparison combining TBQ with R-KV's eviction policy, or vice versa; limited analysis across different cache budgets and batch sizes

strengths: Novel thought-adaptive compression insight: The observation that attention sparsity patterns reveal distinct thought types (R, E, T) with hierarchical importance is well-motivated and clearly demonstrated through empirical analysis (Figures 3-5, Observations 1-3)

Strong and comprehensive empirical results: Achieves near-lossless accuracy (<5% KV cache on multiple benchmarks, <4% drop), 5.8× throughput improvement, and consistent gains across diverse models (R1-Llama 8B/70B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B, AceReason) and datasets (AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500)

Principled algorithm-system co-design: Provides both algorithmic innovation (TBQ, TBE) and practical system solution (Continuous Thinking kernel) that addresses real bottlenecks (gather compaction overhead, memory fragmentation) without expensive operations

Thorough and rigorous evaluation: Includes appropriate baselines (H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction, KIVI, PM-KVQ), ablation studies isolating component contributions (Table 4, Figures 10-11), and diverse experimental settings (batch sizes, compression ratios, multi-user scenarios)

Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear methodology with algorithm specifications (Algorithm 1, Listing 1), detailed walkthroughs (Figure 6, Section D.6), extensive ablations, and proper statistical rigor (8 independent samples, 3 runs averaging)
Addresses critical practical bottleneck: KV cache memory is a real limitation for LRM deployment; the method enables larger batches and prevents OOM failures with achievable implementation
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components (quantization, eviction, attention-based importance) are well-established. The primary contribution is combining them via 'thought decomposition,' which is essentially an empirical observation about attention sparsity rather than a principled theoretical insight lacking theoretical justification for why this decomposition should be universal

Arbitrary design choices with insufficient justification: Fixed |T|=3 lacks principled justification (some models show ambiguous boundaries, §E.4); retention schedule R={64,32,16,8,4} appears hand-tuned with limited sensitivity analysis; τ=128 justified only by empirical observation; treating prefill as R type seems ad-hoc

Thought decomposition methodology concerns: Relies on post-hoc keyword list interpretation (Table 7); calibration requires ~100 labeled prompts with manual threshold extraction via KDE adding complexity; connection between attention sparsity and semantic 'thought' is correlational not causal; limited failure mode analysis

Unclear generalization and limited scope: Primarily evaluated on math/coding reasoning; generalization to other LRM capabilities not demonstrated; §E.10 shows LLM generalization requires different settings (|T|=1), suggesting approach isn't universal; not applicable to long-input scenarios (§F); limited architectural diversity (mostly Llama-based)

Incomplete analysis of extreme compression: At 2.51% cache (95% compression), unclear what prevents collapse—is it only because R tokens dominate with 4-bit precision? Limited ablation on precision assignments (only R4E4T2 vs alternatives). Why does ThinKV avoid 5.1× generation length inflation seen in quantization-only approaches?

Evaluation limitations: 'Near-lossless' claim loose with 1-4% accuracy drops (Table 1, Figure 8); importance scores derived from only 50 rollouts (Figure 4) without error analysis; calibration dataset representativeness unclear; at batch size 1, improvements minimal, suggesting system-level batch utilization plays significant role

Technical concerns inadequately addressed: K-means on post-RoPE embeddings claimed 'negligible drift' within 128 tokens with limited evidence; eviction only at transition boundaries could miss important patterns; some pairwise associations (Figure 5) show unexpected forward dependencies unexplained

Reproducibility gaps: Code availability not mentioned; some hyperparameters appear hand-tuned without principled selection; vLLM integration status and release plans unclear; unclear if modifications will be publicly available for reproducibility

strengths: Addresses important and timely problem of KV cache bottleneck in LRM inference with strong practical results (5.8× throughput, <5% KV cache retention)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model families (8+ models) and benchmarks with thorough ablations and comparisons to reasonable baselines
Thoughtful algorithm-system co-design with Continuous Thinking kernel that practically eliminates gather-based compaction overhead
Extensive reproducibility materials including pseudocode, detailed walkthrough examples, and extensive appendix with visualizations
weaknesses: Core contribution relies on post-hoc, correlational connection between attention sparsity and semantic thought types without rigorous theoretical or causal justification—the three thought types (R,E,T) are identified via keyword matching after observing sparsity, making the reasoning somewhat circular

Limited technical novelty: prior work (Chen et al. 2025b) already identified these thought patterns; using sparsity instead of keywords is an implementation detail. TBQ is straightforward importance-to-precision mapping; TBE uses standard K-means; CT kernel is incremental PagedAttention modification

Critical design choices (|T|=3, precision levels R→8/E→4/T→2, retention schedule, τ=128, min retention=4) justified only empirically without principled justification; some contradictions (§E.4 notes ambiguous boundaries despite fixing |T|=3)

Thought importance (Observation 2) measured on only 2 models, then generalized; sparsity-based inference-time categorization via averaging over L* may obscure important distinctions; online calibration sensitivity unexplored

Evaluation scope limited to math/code reasoning; generalization to other domains unclear. LLM experiments (E.10) require abandoning core contribution (|T|=1). Batch size comparisons sometimes misleading (e.g., Table 2: 5.8× at batch 711 vs 1.6× at iso-batch 256)
Limited failure analysis: only one example of model looping when transitions evicted (E.17); how often does this occur? Insufficient evidence that minimum retention of 4 is universally sufficient

Post-hoc semantic interpretation via keywords (Table 7) not used at inference; unclear what prevents different sparsity patterns on new tasks. Why should attention sparsity universally indicate token importance?

strengths: Strong empirical results across multiple LRM models (R1-Llama, GPT-OSS, AceReason) with <5% KV cache and near-lossless accuracy preservation
Compelling core observation: attention sparsity patterns reveal distinct thought types (R/E/T) validated across models and datasets
Excellent system design addressing gather-based compaction bottleneck; CT kernel achieves 3.2× speedup over sequential gather at iso-batch/iso-compression
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple benchmarks (AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500, GSM8K), thorough ablations (13+ variants), iso-batch/iso-compression comparisons, Pareto-front analysis

Thought-adaptive hybrid approach elegantly combines quantization and eviction, showing better accuracy-compression tradeoff than either alone (Figure 2, Figure 10d shows 5.1× length inflation from quantization alone)
Well-justified algorithmic contributions: K-means clustering for importance-based eviction, group quantization with differentiated precisions, soft-marking for lazy deletion
Strong reproducibility: detailed pseudocode (Listing 1), implementation walkthrough (Figure 6, §D.6), specific format specifications (FP8/NVFP4/Ternary), hyperparameter justification
weaknesses: Thought decomposition generalization concerns: three types (R/E/T) defined post-hoc from observation, not a priori; Figure 14 shows 'hard to distinguish cases' with ambiguous boundaries; §E.4 acknowledges some layers exhibit >3 sparsity regimes; limited analysis of failure modes when sparsity doesn't show tri-modal structure

Lack of theoretical justification for sparsity-to-semantics mapping: why should attention sparsity cleanly correspond to semantic thought structure rather than architectural/training artifacts? No formal connection established beyond empirical correlation

Calibration and generalization: requires offline calibration on 100 prompts; optimal layer selection L* is dataset-specific; sensitivity to calibration set size and robustness to out-of-distribution prompts not demonstrated; threshold transfer across domains unclear

Hyperparameter choices lack strong justification: τ=128 chosen empirically (Figure 10c shows sensitivity but not why this value); retention schedule R={64,32,16,8,4} appears arbitrary with no alternative exploration; K-means complexity in TBE not compared against simpler alternatives; quantization format choices (FP8/NVFP4/Ternary) limited ablation

Insufficient failure mode analysis: §E.17 shows infinite loops when T thoughts evicted but minimum retention=4 is heuristically chosen; no systematic sensitivity analysis; 'outlier T thoughts' mentioned but not characterized; no safety mechanisms beyond threshold

Evaluation scope limitations: only long-output reasoning tasks; §F acknowledges inapplicability to long-input contexts; no evaluation on RAG, summarization, or document understanding; max generation limited to 32K; narrow batch size range (up to 256)

Statistical rigor gaps: results averaged over 3 runs with no error bars or confidence intervals; some accuracy differences (e.g., 76.9% vs 76.4% Table 4) may not be significant; pass@1 inherently high-variance with single samples

Incomplete system analysis: Table 2 shows much throughput gain at batch=256 comes from larger batch size itself, not kernel efficiency; at batch=1 (common in serving), gains marginal vs. FullKV; mechanism for dramatic throughput improvement at large batches not fully explained

Gather overhead analysis platform-specific: Figure 7 only on A100/GH200; HBM characteristics vary across GPUs; overlapped gather interference (Figure 7b) merits deeper investigation; generalization to H100, L4, etc. unclear

Comparison gaps: MiniKV (recent SOTA) mentioned but not in main comparisons; PM-KVQ relegated to Table 1; some baselines designed for LLMs not LRMs; incomplete coverage of recent LRM-specific compression methods
